question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed one-Claw-one-new-agent package, registry, ownership, and lifecycle contract as RFC 0016?
rationale: Patch correctness cannot decide whether these broad and durable product, CLI, manifest, package, provenance, update, and removal surfaces should become supported contracts.

options.title: Accept the contract
options.body: Approve the current experimental design, record its implementation issue, change the RFC status to accepted, and merge it through the normal RFC lifecycle.

options.title: Narrow version one
options.body: Accept the core add and ownership model while deferring selected update, export, MCP, cron, shared-package, or removal guarantees.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the proposal open as draft until the linked implementation series provides more compatibility and upgrade evidence.

recommendation.title: Accept the contract
recommendation.body: Approve the current experimental design, record its implementation issue, change the RFC status to accepted, and merge it through the normal RFC lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history connects this person most directly to the RFC process and acceptance lifecycle, while Patrick-Erichsen remains the strongest product-model reviewer.
